title: Close a handed-back owner's attempt so a daemon restart cannot hold an unassigned row
description:
DEFECT, observed 2026-09-13. A daemon restart can hold a row that nobody owns. While the hold lasts, every explicit-taskId claim of that row is refused with ATTEMPT_RECONCILING, for up to reconcileWindowMs (2h by default).

TIMELINE (task-9e851d4e6e144f808a089bfbbd29ae11)
- 18:43:10Z: qa-64519ef1 claimed the REVIEW row and opened attempt-7cf32d1417084d37814a31cf0610f9e4, generation 2. Generation 1 was closed at the same instant.
- 18:57:36Z: qa_reject moved the row from REVIEW to WORKING and unassigned it. The QA attempt stayed `running`.
- 18:58:52Z: the governor restarted the daemon, with the human's approval, to activate moe.record_check_run. Startup ran reconcileRunningAttempts, which parked the attempt in `reconciling`.
- 19:00-19:01Z: worker-c8e523ea's explicit claim_next_task calls were refused with ATTEMPT_RECONCILING ("task held for qa-64519ef1"). The worker reported the row BLOCKED rather than forcing past the fence.
- 19:08Z: the governor set the row back to WORKING. A ranked claim (no taskId) clears the orphan through the ATTEMPT_ALREADY_OPEN branch of the claim's attempt helper. Explicit claims stay refused until the window sweep closes the attempt.

ROOT CAUSE (packages/moe-daemon/src at main 91e14c2)
1. Hand-back paths never close the outgoing owner's attempt. tools/qaReject.ts, the freeSeat branch of tools/reportBlocked.ts, and tools/setTaskStatus.ts call neither closeOpenAttempts nor anything that calls it. StateManager.updateTask releases the prior owner on a status change, but it does not touch attempts either.
2. Every close path selects tasks by assignedWorkerId, so none of them reaches an orphan. That covers releaseWorkerTasks in state/workerLifecycle.ts (deregister), worker deletion and the startup purge in state/workerStore.ts, and tools/releaseTask.ts, whose repair branch for an unassigned row returns before it reaches closeOpenAttempts.
3. reconcileRunningAttempts in state/attemptStore.ts parks EVERY `running` attempt. It never checks that the task is still assigned to attempt.workerId.
4. The explicit-taskId guard in tools/claimNextTask.ts refuses a claim while any reconciling attempt from another worker exists, even when the row is unassigned.
5. Claims record no processStartedAt or host, so moe.reattach_attempt can never match. Until the runner integration lands, runReconcileWindowSweep in state/sweeps.ts is the only exit.

IMPACT. After any daemon restart, every row that was handed back by qa_reject or by a seat-freeing report_blocked refuses explicit claims for 2h. That includes wrapper RESUME and directed claims. The hold also protects a seat that had already given the row up, which contradicts the documented premise of the restart hold: docs/MCP_SERVER.md, under moe.reattach_attempt, says the spared seat's "task stays WORKING and assigned".

FIX OPTIONS (the architect chooses; A and B together give defence in depth)
A. Close the outgoing owner's open attempts at the moment of hand-back, through the single close path (closeOpenAttempts). The hand-back points are qa_reject, the freeSeat branch of report_blocked, and any status change that clears assignedWorkerId.
B. In reconcileRunningAttempts, close a running attempt instead of parking it when its task is missing or not assigned to attempt.workerId.
C. Symptom only: scope the claim guard to holds whose task is still assigned to the holder. This leaves the orphan attempt open.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do not change the restart hold for an owner that still holds its task (task-58f7db9a's contract and tests).
- Never base a close on lastActivityAt or on any other idle signal.
- Keep the change inside the daemon. Launcher attempt integration belongs to task-49ec8755.

RELATED OBSERVATION from the same incident; the architect decides whether it is in scope or becomes a separate card. assertWorkerOwns in util/enforcement.ts returns early for an unassigned task, so moe.start_step succeeds for a worker that never claimed the row. tools/startStep.ts then stamps that worker CODING with currentTaskId. That is how worker-c8e523ea ended up with a stale back-pointer to a row it never held.

RELATED CARDS
- task-b6c48bf029bf4170a603a91c12451df7: open and close attempts on the claim and release paths.
- task-58f7db9a9e44469e9351b2cdea73b47d: restart reconciliation.
- task-d7fa98f4e43d434a96cad9440b153f1c: window sweep.
- The epic integration pass, task-808869c56228430ca5b15cb901497544, may want this card as a dependency.

EVIDENCE
- #general msg-5fdd35aee2c94cb4b4a2732358b5092c and msg-1896691588f64257a51be38daa389fd1
- #governors msg-6f475cab5505468a837ed6efe7060312
- Governor comment comment-9c5eb13927df40669a704295bc5d39c2 on task-9e851
- .moe/attempts/attempt-7cf32d1417084d37814a31cf0610f9e4.json
definitionOfDone: A task handed back by qa_reject, by report_blocked's seat-freeing branch, or by any status change that clears assignedWorkerId keeps no open attempt owned by the seat that gave it up

After daemon startup reconciliation, no reconciling attempt holds a task that is unassigned or assigned to a different worker, and an explicit-taskId claim_next_task by another worker on such a row succeeds

The restart hold for a still-assigned owner is unchanged: its running attempt is parked in reconciling and third-party explicit claims are still refused with ATTEMPT_RECONCILING (existing restart-hold tests stay green)

A regression test reproduces the 2026-09-13 incident: QA claims a REVIEW row, qa_reject, restart reconciliation plus purge, then another worker's explicit claim of that row succeeds with a strictly greater generation
docs/MCP_SERVER.md documents the close-on-hand-back rule and which attempts a restart parks; npm test and npx tsc --noEmit pass in packages/moe-daemon
taskRails: Never close or release an attempt based on lastActivityAt or any other idle signal
Daemon-only: do not edit scripts/moe-agent.ps1 or scripts/moe-agent.sh (task-49ec8755 owns launcher attempt integration)

implementationPlan.description: Phase 1+2 — Confirm the chain on disk before editing (no code changes in this step; post ONE task comment with the findings). Verify at main: attemptStore.ts reconcileRunningAttempts (~350-364) filters on phase==='running' only; taskStore.ts updateTask (~310-351) nulls assignedWorkerId on a status change (shouldClearWorker), writes the task at ~332, releases the prior owner at ~342-351 and never touches attempts; claimNextTask.ts explicit-taskId guard (~262-274) refuses on holding.workerId !== params.workerId without reading task.assignedWorkerId (the task is fetched only at ~278); workerStore.ts workersHoldingOpenAttempts (~320-327) spares by phase only and the purge's close (~438-450) runs only inside the assigned-task loop (~412-413); hand-back writers qaReject.ts (~230-276; the parked arm writes null explicitly at ~250), reportBlocked.ts seat-freeing arm (~299-310, omits assignedWorkerId on purpose), setTaskStatus.ts (~164-198, keeps the seat only on the two BLOCKED edges), unblockWorker.ts (~96-112, explicit null, no status change) — none import attemptStore. Then confirm three facts this plan relies on: (a) MUTEX — attemptStore enforces nothing ('The store cannot enforce that alone', header ~14-18); the only introspection is AsyncMutex.isHeld() (StateManager.ts ~296); every updateTask caller that can turn a non-null assignedWorkerId into null already runs under the mutex (McpAdapter non-blocking dispatch ~301, WebSocketServer withMutex ~232, sweeps.ts ~292/~352, releaseTask.ts runExclusive ~174, submitPlan.ts SPEED timer ~54, waitForResource.ts ~82, workerStore.ts deleteWorker ~233, enterGovernance.ts ~114, deregisterWorker.ts ~27, index.ts ~506-507); the only updateTask callers outside the mutex are backfillTaskMetrics.ts ~131 and StateManager.ts ~1457, which never write assignedWorkerId. Therefore step 5 takes the plain chokepoint route with NO isHeld() gate — such a gate would also make step 2's tests silently skip the close, because the harness calls tool handlers outside the mutex. (b) RETURN VALUE — no src consumer of closeOpenAttempts' result exists (releaseTask.ts ~338, workerLifecycle.ts ~146, claimNextTask.ts ~70/400/416, workerStore.ts ~273/446 all discard it; claimNextTask.test.ts ~1231 uses it as a seed only), so the double-closes step 5 creates are safe. (c) WRAPPER CONSEQUENCE (record it, do NOT edit the wrappers — task rail): scripts/moe-agent.sh finalize_postflight (~6733) calls finalize_attempt_rpc (~1968-1973) whose moe_attempt_read (~1872-1888) returns 1 when the task has no non-closed attempt owned by this worker, which sets POSTFLIGHT_BREAK and leaves the claim loop (~6797-6799); the ps1 twin is Read-MoeAttempt (~1279) / Send-MoeFinalize (~1363). release_task already produces that shape today; after this task a WORKER seat's seat-freeing report_blocked, a human set_task_status or a seat-only unblock_worker mid-session will end that wrapper's loop after its checkpoint landing instead of claiming other work. The wrapper fix is filed as task-e47284ef038c423b85a2ebd304e0f4a6 (BACKLOG, this epic) and the start_step ownership hole as task-c628902ee8ba45188660e7a28f0e0bdd; cite both ids in the comment.

implementationPlan.description: Phase 3 — Tests first: hand-back and the incident regression, in a NEW file packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptHandback.test.ts. Idioms: `const h = new ToolTestHarness(); h.init(); h.setupMoeFolder({ schemaVersion: 6 }); h.createEpic(); h.createTask({...}); await h.state.load();` (see workerStore.test.ts ~24-37 and toolTestHarness.ts); import attempts from './attemptStore.js' (this file lives in src/state/) and tools from '../tools/<tool>.js'; invoke handlers directly as <x>Tool(h.state).handler(args, h.state); `h.state.clearEmitter()` before `h.cleanup()`. Assert with `listAttempts(h.state, taskId).map(a => [a.generation, a.phase])` and exact error `codeName` — never a bare truthy check. Cases marked RED must fail on current main; cases marked GUARD are green before and after and exist so a regression in the other direction fails. (1) RED qa_reject: QA claims a REVIEW row by explicit taskId (the claim opens the attempt and auto-registers the worker; stamp contextFetchedBy via getContextTool with the QA workerId), qa_reject with a reason (no delivery candidate recorded, reopenCount 0 stays under the soft cap so the destination is WORKING) → task WORKING + unassigned, QA worker IDLE, the QA attempt 'closed'. (2) RED report_blocked seat-freeing arm (no resourceId, reported by the assignee) closes the worker's running attempt and marks the worker IDLE; GUARD resource-parked arm — the assignee must have a worker record (h.createWorker or claim first), because that arm calls state.updateWorker(assignee, { status: BLOCKED }) which throws Worker not found for a bare createTask({ assignedWorkerId }) fixture (reportBlocked.test.ts ~297-331 is the working shape); first hold the resource from ANOTHER task via acquire_resource { resourceId, taskId, workerId } (a free resource is granted without a flip, reportBlocked.ts ~99-133), then report_blocked with that resourceId flips the task BLOCKED with the seat kept, marks the assignee BLOCKED (reportBlocked.ts ~340-341) and the attempt stays 'running'. (3) RED set_task_status WORKING→BACKLOG closes the attempt; GUARD WORKING→BLOCKED and BLOCKED→blockedFromStatus preserve the assignee and leave it open. (4) RED unblock_worker seat-only arm: unblock_worker refuses unless worker.status === 'BLOCKED' (unblockWorker.ts ~43-50), so reach that state through case (2)'s resource-parked arm or `h.state.updateWorker(id, { status: 'BLOCKED' })`, then call unblock_worker WITHOUT retryTask/resolveBlocks — the seat-only arm writes assignedWorkerId: null with no status change (~107-111), which is exactly the explicit-null write the chokepoint must key on → attempt 'closed', task stays BLOCKED. (5) GUARD complete_task (with verification { command, exitCode: 0 }) → REVIEW leaves the attempt in 'finalizing' — the seat clear must not close a finalizing attempt (assert phase === 'finalizing'). (6) RED INCIDENT REGRESSION (DoD 4): REVIEW row with a closed generation-1 attempt (openAttempt then setAttemptPhase 'closed'); QA explicit claim returns generation 2; get_context stamp; qa_reject → WORKING/unassigned; BACKDATE the QA seat before the restart because purgeAllWorkers also keeps every seat whose lastActivityAt is within 120s (`await h.state.updateWorker(qaId, { lastActivityAt: <3h ago ISO> })`, an explicit value is honoured, workerStore.ts ~185-187); then the restart passes in daemon order `await reconcileRunningAttempts(h.state); await h.state.purgeAllWorkers();` (index.ts ~506-507); then worker-2's explicit claim { statuses: ['WORKING'], taskId, workerId: 'worker-2' } succeeds: hasNext true, generation 3, phases exactly [[1,'closed'],[2,'closed'],[3,'running']], task assigned to worker-2, no non-closed attempt names the QA worker, and the QA worker record is gone from state.workers. (7) RED guard scoping: create the WORKING row UNASSIGNED via h.createTask before load (never by clearing a seat through updateTask, which step 5 would turn into a close), openAttempt for qa-1 and park it with setAttemptPhase 'reconciling' → worker-2's explicit claim succeeds with the successor generation and the orphan reads 'closed'; GUARD mirror with the row still assigned to qa-1 (qa-1 registered) stays refused with codeName ATTEMPT_RECONCILING (as workerStore.test.ts ~206).

implementationPlan.description: Phase 4a — attemptStore.ts (+ two comment-only edits elsewhere). (1) Add `export async function closeHandedBackAttempts(state: StateManager, taskId: string): Promise<ExecutionAttempt[]>` beside closeOpenAttempts (~387-397): same mutex precondition, same idempotent loop over listAttempts(state, taskId), but it closes ONLY phases 'running' and 'reconciling' — NEVER 'finalizing', because completeTask.ts (~149-156) parks the attempt in finalizing BEFORE its own REVIEW updateTask clears the seat, and that hold is lifted only by moe.finalize_attempt (say so in the doc comment). (2) reconcileRunningAttempts (~350-364): for each 'running' attempt look up `state.getTask(attempt.taskId)`; PARK (setAttemptPhase 'reconciling') only when the task exists and `task.assignedWorkerId === attempt.workerId`; otherwise CLOSE it (setAttemptPhase 'closed') and log at info with { attemptId, taskId, workerId, assignedWorkerId } — the orphan closed at boot. Keep the per-attempt try/catch (error handling: one bad record never stops the loop) and the return value as the list of PARKED attempts (index.ts and workerStore.test.ts ~132-151 depend on it). Error handling for the close arm — give it its own catch/log text: a close that fails leaves the orphan 'running' on an unassigned row, which is benign — the row is not held (step 6's guard keys on 'reconciling') and the next claim closes it through openClaimAttempt's ATTEMPT_ALREADY_OPEN arm; the existing park-arm message ('its task stays held') must not be reused for it. Never consult lastActivityAt, presenceAt or any idle signal (task rail). (3) Comment sweep: the header comments in attemptStore.ts (~323-349 boot rule, ~366-386 list of close sites, add 'seat hand-back via taskStore.updateTask'), plus the two places that repeat 'a restart parks every running attempt': sweeps.ts ~174-175 and workerStore.ts ~330-336 (comment-only edits; no code change in those two files). Make step 3's tests green.

implementationPlan.description: Phase 4b — taskStore.ts updateTask: close on hand-back at the single chokepoint every seat-clearing write already shares, and re-seed the one sweep fixture that relied on the leak. In updateTask (~225-394), between the prior-owner release (~342-351) and appendActivity/emit (~356-361, so TASK_UPDATED publishes after the close), when the write turned a NON-NULL assignedWorkerId into null — whether through the shouldClearWorker status-change cascade or an explicit `assignedWorkerId: null` (qaReject's parked arm, unblock_worker's seat-only arm, handBackUnrecordedClaim in claimNextTask.ts ~82, the REVIEW self-heal sweeps.ts ~464 and dependency-waiting release ~417, all of which write null with NO status change so shouldClearWorker is false for them) — call closeHandedBackAttempts(state, taskId). Key on the before/after values of assignedWorkerId, never on shouldClearWorker. Do nothing for null→worker (claims), worker→worker, or same-worker writes, and nothing when the seat is kept (resource-parked report_blocked, the BLOCKED edges in set_task_status, a dependency/resource restore that keeps the same worker). A restore that returns the row unassigned because the recorded owner is missing, DEAD or moved on (dependencyUnblock.ts ~221-233, resourceStore.ts ~338-351 restoreTo=null) IS a hand-back and closes like any other — that is intended. Error handling: wrap the close in try/catch that logs and continues — the task write is already durable and a failed close must not fail the tool (the boot rule from step 4 heals it on the next restart). taskStore.updateTask receives the StateManager instance and attemptStore imports StateManager as a type only, so no runtime cycle is introduced (stateModules.test.ts guards this). The explicit closeOpenAttempts calls at releaseTask.ts ~338, workerLifecycle.ts ~146 and claimNextTask.ts ~400/416 stay as idempotent no-op double-closes (setAttemptPhase returns early on a same-phase re-assert); purgeAllWorkers bypasses updateTask via writeEntity and keeps its own close — leave both. FIXTURE: sweeps.test.ts 'closes a stale attempt but never yanks a row a different worker now holds' (~294-311) hands the row back through `updateTask('task-L', { assignedWorkerId: null })` (~301) before reassigning to worker-Z and then asserts the window sweep's return equals ['attempt-L-1'] — after this step that write closes the attempt first and the sweep returns []. Re-seed the fixture so the mismatch exists without a seat-clearing write: create task-L already assigned to worker-Z (with worker-Z's record) before load, open attempt-L-1 for worker-W and park it via setAttemptPhase 'reconciling' + the file's backdatePhase helper; the never-yank branch and its ['attempt-L-1'] return still hold. Do NOT narrow the phase filter of closeHandedBackAttempts to keep the old fixture green — that would reopen DoD 2 and case (7). Make step 2's cases (1)-(5) green.

(1) Hand-back racing a claim. Every seat-clearing updateTask caller runs under the state mutex (step 1a), and claim_next_task runs in runExclusive, so the two serialize.
- Hand-back first: the hook closes gen N inside that write, and the claim finds nothing open and opens N+1.
- Claim first: a third party's claim of a still-assigned row is refused and writes nothing. With replaceExisting, the eviction's updateTask(null) closes N through the hook (closeOpenAttempts closes any finalizing), the claimer gets N+1, and the old owner's qa_reject is refused by assertWorkerOwns.

(2) Double close. release_task, releaseWorkerTasks, deleteWorker and both claim-eviction branches all write through updateTask first. - Failed park: the attempt stays running, held and spared, as before ('survives an attempt it cannot park').

completionSummary:
A daemon restart can no longer hold a row that nobody owns. Three layers, all under the state mutex:
(1) CHOKEPOINT. taskStore.updateTask calls closeAttemptsOnHandBack -> attemptStore.closeHandedBackAttempts on every write that turns a non-null assignedWorkerId into null (a status-change clear or an explicit null). It closes running and reconciling attempts only; finalizing survives until finalize_attempt. A failed close is logged, never thrown.
(2) BOOT RULE. reconcileRunningAttempts parks a running attempt only when its task still exists and is assigned to that attempt's worker. It closes every running or reconciling attempt whose task is missing, unassigned or assigned elsewhere, so the purge no longer spares that seat.
